newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel threat said to hang over Colombian capital.
newsitem.headline: Rebel threat said to hang over Colombian capital.

text.p: Colombia's defence minister was quoted on Saturday as saying leftist guerrillas planned to unleash a series of attacks in Bogota to cap their bloodiest offensive in decades.
The minister, Juan Carlos Esguerra, told the El Espectador newspaper the planned spiral in rebel activity had been uncovered by military intelligence and was expected to take place over the weekend.
He added that "precautionary measures" had been put in place, however, and that "any possible subversive action" would be quickly contained.
U.S. citizens in Colombia were warned in a circular issued by the American consulate on Friday not to stray outside of the capital until further notice.
The warning referred to the threat of a surge in "subversive operations" in and around Bogota and said all Americans had been advised not to travel outside the city limits.

About 100 Colombian soliders and police have been killed since Aug. 30 in the most dramatic offensive since the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia and National Liberation Army -- the country's two largest guerrilla groups -- were founded in the mid-1960s.

More than 60 soldiers have been seized as "prisoners of war" as part of the offensive, which appeared to catch military commanders completely off guard and has sparked heated debate about the failures of army intelligence and preparedness after more than three decades of guerrilla war.
